speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in view of the global spread of COVID-19 (a) what is the estimated economic impact on Singapore's GDP; (b) whether there has been a decrease in capital inflows; and (c) whether adjustments to forecasts on job creation are expected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: First, it has led to a sharp fall in tourist arrivals, particularly from China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This affects our tourism, transport, retail and food and beverage (F&B) sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Second, domestic consumption in Singapore has declined as locals cut back on activities, such as shopping and eating out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Third, the outbreak will dampen economic growth in several of our key markets, especially China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This affects export-oriented sectors, including manufacturing and wholesale trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These sectors are also affected by supply chain disruptions due to factory closures and labour shortages in China, due to the lockdowns and travel restrictions imposed by the Chinese government to contain the outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Regional financial markets, including Singapore, have seen greater volatility amidst heightened uncertainty and concerns over the spread of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In Singapore, prices for equities and bonds denominated in Singapore dollars have fallen and the nominal exchange rate of the Singapore dollar has eased, in line with weaker economic conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, we know the COVID-19 situation is still evolving, and the total impact on our economy will depend on the length and severity of the outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation closely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, there will be an impact on our companies and workers in the near term, especially in the more badly affected sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government will work together with employers and our unions to support our companies and save jobs for our workers during this difficult period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is what our tripartite partnership is about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We stand together with our brothers and sisters, and we help one another through thick and thin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I was glad to receive a message from a business leader who owns a chain of restaurants in Singapore and the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: He had advised other employers in his industry that, "Most important, keep the team intact for you will need them to be ready for the recovery." When we met the Singapore Hotels Association – as you know hotels are one of the sectors that are badly affected – the hotel owners and general managers fully supported working with the Government and unions to keep their workers employed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I witnessed the same solidarity and support from our union leaders at a recent dialogue at the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These examples and many others give me the confidence that, as a nation, we can and we will, overcome this crisis together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government has announced some measures to help those who are most affected by the outbreak, such as the tourism and transport sectors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first is on the packages of support for affected workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It has been very warmly received by our workers in the transport sector, especially our taxi drivers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We do expect some impact on the manufacturing sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would there be support for this group of workers with some immediacy?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second one is on the delays in new investments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With the current situation in China and regional areas, do we expect new investments in Singapore to be delayed?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While they are not going to be cancelled, but do we expect the delays resulting in job creation, only coming down, further down the line, rather than in the coming few months?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The third one is that with the Singapore dollar easing and with exports of materials coming slower from China, do we expect then to have some inflationary pressure in the coming few months?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For other measures, the Minister for Finance will address these in the Budget Statement.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In fact, I would make an argument that how we deal with the current situation will affect how investors see Singapore in time to come.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we can deal with this calmly, cohesively, and show the world that Singapore, we have what it takes to inspire confidence and to deal with the situation in a professional manner and to bounce back and emerge stronger, then we can turn this crisis into an opportunity to differentiate ourselves from our competitors.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And it actually brings the point to bear that that is why we need to ensure that our supply sources are diversified.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why we need to ensure that our supply chains are resilient.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is why we also need to diversify our economic structure, our sectors and our markets.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is a very useful reminder, not just for companies in Singapore, but companies throughout the world, that diversification, supply chain resilience, are all very important medium- to longer-term considerations.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We should, even after we deal with this crisis, continue to press on with our restructuring efforts to improve our competitiveness to upgrade the skills of our workers, to transform our enterprises.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: China is a country where many Singapore companies have successfully internationalised into.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the grim situation in the Chinese economy now, can I ask the Senior Minister of State what does he see the impact to our Singapore companies in China, and whether there are ways and means that we can also assist them?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Companies that have workers who are currently in China, they have to come back in batches, because we need to make sure that we are able to protect public safety when these workers come back.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Companies that have businesses in China are also being affected by the measures that are implemented in China to contain the outbreak.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we look beyond the near-term, the prospects for companies to invest overseas, to expand their operations overseas, including in China, I think that still remains an attractive market.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This approach of having a diversified supply chain, diversified market, is still the best medium- to longer-term strategy to develop our economy and to grow our businesses.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Yesterday, several contractors told me that they have Bangladeshi workers who wanted to go home, to leave the worksite and go back because some of the cases involved Bangladeshi workers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask whether our Ministry is going to take any action to educate the workers to share with them so that they will continue to work in Singapore.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because this contractor says that if all these workers decide to leave Singapore, they cannot operate.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I am sure this is something which the Government agencies will continue to work closely with employers to raise awareness, to educate our workers that the work environment that they are in will be safe and, therefore, there is no need for them to worry.
